To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of a solubilizate solubilized in a micelle is a function of the polarity of the solubilizate.
the solubilization of benzoic acids by polysorbate 10 and 20 micelles is a function of the polarity of the solubilizate and the concentration of the surfactant.
the solubility of benzoic acids increases with increasing surfactant concentration in the micellar solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of benzoic acids of varying polarity with polysorbate micelles in aqueous media at controlled pH.
the interaction of substituted benzoates with the nonionic surfactant, polysorbate 80.
the interaction of substituted benzoate ions with polysorbate micelles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the partitioning of benzoic acids between aqueous and polysorbate 2 micelles depends on the degree of ionization, the degree of solubilizate solubilization, and the polarity of the solubilizate molecule.
the solubilizing power of the polysorbate 30 micelles is dependent upon the polarity of the solubilizate and that the micellar environment is more polar than the aqueous environment.
the solubility of a solubilizate in a micellar phase is a function of its partitioning into the micellar phase and the solubility in the aqueous phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solubilizing ability of polysorbate is related to the partitioning of the solubilized species between the aqueous and micelle phases and to the polarity of solubilized molecules.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the micellar solubilization of benzoic acids is governed by the same principles that govern their solubility in water, and the micellar solvation of these molecules can be predicted using the same approach used for water.
the micellar solubilization capacity for benzoic acids increases as the number of hydroxyl groups on the benzene ring increases.
